answer: A proposed sonnet archive admits a paid key only after sealing its own 2-TiB island of chained, key-salted pages. Independent verifiers broadcast a fresh zephyr nonce and require 64 random Merkle openings from every key within 200 ms; missing or reused proofs forfeit that epoch's pay. A farm's cheapest move is shared encoding plus rented disks, but each added clone still occupies a separate live 2 TiB through simultaneous surprise audits. If it stores only a seed, chained recomputation misses the deadline; borrowing disks cannot make one copy serve two keys. MinePoA has no such rule.
